name: Acadia
facts: Cadillac Mountain is, for part of the year, one of the first places in the continental United States to see the sunrise.
The park protects approximately 49,000 acres of coastal landscape in Maine.

name: American Samoa
facts: It is the only U.S. national park south of the equator, protecting paleotropical rainforest and coral reefs across three volcanic islands.
The park protects approximately 8,300 acres of island tropical landscape in American Samoa.
visitorCenters: National Park of American Samoa Visitor Center

name: Arches
facts: Arches contains over 2,000 documented natural sandstone arches, the highest density of them in the world.
The park protects approximately 76,700 acres of desert landscape in Utah.

name: Badlands
facts: The park's striped rock layers hold one of the richest Oligocene-epoch mammal fossil beds in the world.
The park protects approximately 242,800 acres of desert landscape in South Dakota.

name: Big Bend
facts: Big Bend hosts more bird species, around 450, than any other U.S. national park.
The park protects approximately 801,000 acres of desert landscape in Texas.

name: Biscayne
facts: About 95 percent of the park is open water, protecting a long stretch of Florida's living coral reef.
The park protects approximately 173,000 acres of coastal landscape in Florida.

name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison
facts: The canyon's Painted Wall is Colorado's tallest cliff, rising about 2,250 feet from river to rim.
The park protects approximately 30,800 acres of canyon landscape in Colorado.

name: Bryce Canyon
facts: Bryce Canyon contains the largest concentration of hoodoos found anywhere on Earth.
The park protects approximately 35,800 acres of canyon landscape in Utah.

name: Canyonlands
facts: The confluence of the Green and Colorado Rivers splits the park into three distinct districts: Island in the Sky, The Needles, and The Maze.
The park protects approximately 337,600 acres of canyon landscape in Utah.
visitorCenters: Island in the Sky Visitor Center

name: Capitol Reef
facts: The park protects the Waterpocket Fold, a nearly 100-mile-long wrinkle in the earth's crust.
The park protects approximately 241,900 acres of canyon landscape in Utah.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
facts: The Big Room chamber is one of the largest single cave chambers by volume in North America.
The park protects approximately 46,800 acres of desert landscape in New Mexico.

name: Channel Islands
facts: The park is home to the island fox, a species found nowhere else on Earth and roughly the size of a housecat.
The park protects approximately 249,600 acres of coastal landscape in California.

name: Congaree
facts: Congaree protects the largest intact expanse of old-growth bottomland hardwood forest left in the United States, with some of the tallest trees in eastern North America.
The park protects approximately 26,700 acres of wetland landscape in South Carolina.

name: Crater Lake
facts: Formed by the collapse of ancient Mount Mazama, Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States at 1,943 feet.
The park protects approximately 183,200 acres of volcanic landscape in Oregon.

name: Cuyahoga Valley
facts: The park was established around the Cuyahoga River, whose 1969 fire helped spark the modern environmental movement.
The park protects approximately 32,600 acres of forest landscape in Ohio.

name: Death Valley
facts: Badwater Basin, at 282 feet below sea level, is the lowest point in North America, and Death Valley holds the record for the hottest air temperature ever recorded on Earth.
The park protects approximately 3,408,000 acres of desert landscape in California, Nevada.

name: Denali
facts: Denali is the tallest peak in North America, rising to 20,310 feet.
The park protects approximately 4,741,000 acres of alpine landscape in Alaska.

name: Dry Tortugas
facts: The park's centerpiece, Fort Jefferson, is the largest all-masonry fort in the Western Hemisphere, built from over 16 million bricks.
The park protects approximately 64,700 acres of island tropical landscape in Florida.

name: Everglades
facts: Everglades is the only place on Earth where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.
The park protects approximately 1,509,000 acres of wetland landscape in Florida.

name: Gates of the Arctic
facts: Gates of the Arctic has no roads or maintained trails anywhere in the park, making it the least-visited national park in the United States.
The park protects approximately 7,524,000 acres of arctic tundra landscape in Alaska.

name: Gateway Arch
facts: At 630 feet tall, the Gateway Arch is the tallest man-made monument in the Western Hemisphere.
The park protects approximately 193 acres of forest landscape in Missouri.

name: Glacier
facts: The park had more than 100 named glaciers in 1850; fewer than 25 remain today.
The park protects approximately 1,013,100 acres of alpine landscape in Montana.

name: Glacier Bay
facts: The bay was almost entirely covered by a single tidewater glacier as recently as 1750; the ice has since retreated more than 65 miles.
The park protects approximately 3,223,400 acres of coastal landscape in Alaska.

name: Grand Canyon
facts: The canyon exposes nearly two billion years of Earth's geologic history in its layered rock walls.
The park protects approximately 1,201,600 acres of canyon landscape in Arizona.

name: Grand Teton
facts: The Teton Range has no foothills, so the peaks appear to rise abruptly straight from the valley floor.
The park protects approximately 310,000 acres of alpine landscape in Wyoming.
visitorCenters: Craig Thomas Discovery and Visitor Center

name: Great Basin
facts: The park protects groves of Great Basin bristlecone pines, some of the oldest living non-clonal trees on Earth at over 4,000 years old.
The park protects approximately 77,200 acres of desert landscape in Nevada.

name: Great Sand Dunes
facts: Great Sand Dunes contains the tallest sand dunes in North America, with Star Dune rising nearly 750 feet.
The park protects approximately 107,300 acres of desert landscape in Colorado.

name: Great Smoky Mountains
facts: It is the most visited national park in the United States, drawing more than twice the visitors of any other.
The park protects approximately 522,400 acres of forest landscape in North Carolina, Tennessee.

name: Guadalupe Mountains
facts: Guadalupe Peak, at 8,751 feet, is the highest point in Texas.
The park protects approximately 86,400 acres of desert landscape in Texas.

name: Haleakalā
facts: Haleakalā's massive volcanic crater is so barren and otherworldly that NASA has used it to test lunar and Mars rover equipment.
The park protects approximately 33,500 acres of volcanic landscape in Hawaii.

name: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes
facts: The park protects Kīlauea, one of the most active volcanoes on Earth.
The park protects approximately 344,800 acres of volcanic landscape in Hawaii.

name: Hot Springs
facts: Land here was first federally protected in 1832, making it the oldest area in the National Park System, decades before Yellowstone.
The park protects approximately 5,550 acres of forest landscape in Arkansas.

name: Indiana Dunes
facts: Because it sits where several ecosystems converge along Lake Michigan, the park has one of the highest levels of plant biodiversity of any U.S. national park.
The park protects approximately 15,350 acres of coastal landscape in Indiana.
visitorCenters: Paul H. Douglas Center for Environmental Education

name: Isle Royale
facts: The island is home to the longest continuous predator-prey study in the world, tracking wolves and moose since 1958.
The park protects approximately 571,800 acres of forest landscape in Michigan.

name: Joshua Tree
facts: The park sits at the meeting point of the Mojave and Colorado deserts, each with distinct plant life.
The park protects approximately 795,200 acres of desert landscape in California.

name: Katmai
hikes: Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes hike
facts: Katmai formed around the 1912 eruption of Novarupta, the largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century, and is now famous for brown bears fishing at Brooks Falls.
The park protects approximately 3,674,500 acres of volcanic landscape in Alaska.

name: Kenai Fjords
facts: The park protects the Harding Icefield, one of the largest ice fields in the United States, which feeds nearly 40 glaciers.
The park protects approximately 669,600 acres of coastal landscape in Alaska.
visitorCenters: Kenai Fjords National Park Visitor Center

name: Kings Canyon
facts: The park's General Grant Tree is the second-largest tree on Earth by volume.
The park protects approximately 461,900 acres of forest landscape in California.

name: Kobuk Valley
hikes: Great Kobuk Sand Dunes cross-country hike
facts: Nearly half a million caribou migrate through the park's Great Kobuk Sand Dunes twice a year, and the park has no roads or maintained trails.
The park protects approximately 1,750,700 acres of arctic tundra landscape in Alaska.

name: Lake Clark
facts: Lake Clark has no road access, reachable only by small plane or boat, and contains two active volcanoes, Redoubt and Iliamna.
The park protects approximately 2,619,800 acres of alpine landscape in Alaska.

name: Lassen Volcanic
facts: Lassen Peak, one of the largest plug dome volcanoes in the world, last erupted in 1915, prompting the park's creation the following year.
The park protects approximately 106,600 acres of volcanic landscape in California.

name: Mammoth Cave
facts: Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world, with over 420 mapped miles of passages.
The park protects approximately 72,500 acres of forest landscape in Kentucky.

name: Mesa Verde
facts: The park protects nearly 5,000 archaeological sites, including about 600 cliff dwellings built by Ancestral Puebloans.
The park protects approximately 52,500 acres of canyon landscape in Colorado.
visitorCenters: Mesa Verde Visitor and Research Center

name: Mount Rainier
facts: Mount Rainier is the most heavily glaciated peak in the contiguous United States, carrying 25 major glaciers.
The park protects approximately 236,400 acres of alpine landscape in Washington.
visitorCenters: Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center

name: New River Gorge
facts: It is the newest U.S. national park, redesignated from a national river in 2020, and its gorge bridge is one of the longest steel single-span arch bridges in the world.
The park protects approximately 7,000 acres of canyon landscape in West Virginia.

name: North Cascades
facts: North Cascades contains over 300 glaciers, more than any other U.S. national park outside Alaska.
The park protects approximately 504,800 acres of alpine landscape in Washington.

name: Olympic
facts: Olympic National Park contains three strikingly different ecosystems in one park: glaciated mountains, temperate rainforest, and rugged Pacific coastline.
The park protects approximately 922,600 acres of forest landscape in Washington.

name: Petrified Forest
facts: The park holds one of the largest concentrations of petrified wood in the world, some logs over 200 million years old.
The park protects approximately 221,400 acres of desert landscape in Arizona.

name: Pinnacles
facts: The park's rock spires are eroded remnants of an ancient volcanic field, and it is a key release site for the endangered California condor.
The park protects approximately 26,700 acres of volcanic landscape in California.

name: Redwood
facts: Redwood National and State Parks protect the tallest trees on Earth, including specimens over 350 feet high.
The park protects approximately 139,000 acres of forest landscape in California.

name: Rocky Mountain
facts: Trail Ridge Road, which crosses the park, is the highest continuous paved through-road in the United States.
The park protects approximately 265,800 acres of alpine landscape in Colorado.

name: Saguaro
facts: The park protects dense stands of saguaro cactus, which can live over 150 years and grow taller than 40 feet.
The park protects approximately 91,700 acres of desert landscape in Arizona.

name: Sequoia
facts: Sequoia is home to General Sherman, the largest known tree on Earth by trunk volume.
The park protects approximately 404,000 acres of forest landscape in California.

name: Shenandoah
facts: The Appalachian Trail runs through Shenandoah for about 101 miles, more than through any other national park.
The park protects approximately 199,200 acres of forest landscape in Virginia.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
facts: The park is named for Theodore Roosevelt, who ranched in these North Dakota badlands as a young man, an experience that shaped his conservation legacy.
The park protects approximately 70,400 acres of desert landscape in North Dakota.

name: Virgin Islands
facts: The park protects Trunk Bay's famous underwater snorkeling trail along with the ruins of 18th-century Danish sugar plantations.
The park protects approximately 15,000 acres of island tropical landscape in U.S. Virgin Islands.
visitorCenters: Annaberg Historic District Visitor Contact Station

name: Voyageurs
facts: Named for French-Canadian fur traders who once paddled its waterways, roughly a third of the park's area is open water.
The park protects approximately 218,000 acres of forest landscape in Minnesota.

name: White Sands
facts: White Sands protects the largest gypsum dune field on Earth, covering nearly 275 square miles.
The park protects approximately 146,500 acres of desert landscape in New Mexico.

name: Wind Cave
facts: Wind Cave is one of the longest and most complex cave systems in the world and holds most of the world's known boxwork cave formations.
The park protects approximately 28,300 acres of forest landscape in South Dakota.

name: Wrangell-St. Elias
facts: At over 8.3 million acres, Wrangell-St. Elias is the largest national park in the United States, roughly the size of Switzerland.
The park protects approximately 8,332,600 acres of alpine landscape in Alaska.

name: Yellowstone
facts: Established in 1872, Yellowstone was the world's first national park and sits atop one of the largest active volcanic systems on Earth.
The park protects approximately 2,213,000 acres of volcanic landscape in Wyoming, Montana, Idaho.

name: Yosemite
facts: Yosemite's El Capitan is one of the largest granite monoliths in the world and a mecca for rock climbers.
The park protects approximately 761,700 acres of alpine landscape in California.

name: Zion
facts: The Zion Narrows is one of the narrowest slot canyons in the world carved by a river, in places just 20-30 feet wide with walls 1,000 feet tall.
The park protects approximately 147,200 acres of canyon landscape in Utah.
